01.r: Introduces one group among the complaining people.
01.n: The word is a noun meaning being or existence, used for 'there is'. Gesenius calls its use for the verb 'to be', without distinction of number or tense, by far the most common; the past tense here comes from the story.

02.n: BDB notes that this particle can include its own antecedent, so 'who' here means 'those who'.

03.r: What this group was saying at the time.
03.n: A participle: a description of what they were saying, not a single remark.

04.n: The KJV and Geneva say 'lands'. The Hebrew order puts the property first, before the verb, for emphasis.

05.r: Their planted vineyards, a second kind of property.
05.n: Gesenius gives the first sense as a field set with plants of nobler quality, cultivated as a garden or orchard.

07.n: The pronoun is written out, which the brief's lexicon notes is usually for emphasis.

08.r: They are putting their property up as security for loans.
08.n: BDB: take on pledge, give in pledge, exchange, and go surety for. The translations' 'mortgaging' gives the sense: the land stands behind a debt. A participle, so something going on at the time; YLT keeps it with 'we are pledging'.

09.r: Their resolve: to get grain with what the pledges raise.
09.n: A cohortative, first person plural: 'let us take', a form of resolve; the prefix נ and the ending ה mark it. The verb is the common 'take', as wide as English 'take' or 'get'; the KJV makes it 'buy'.

10.n: Gesenius: corn, and used of bread. 'Corn' in older English meant grain of any kind.

11.r: The time of scarcity in which they speak.
11.n: Gesenius: hunger, famine, whether of individuals or of whole provinces, scarcity of grain. The Hebrew has 'in', of the time; the KJV and others make it the cause, 'because of the dearth'.

_extra.17: καὶ (and): begins a phrase added in the Greek, 'and we shall eat'.
_extra.18: φαγόμεθα (we shall eat): the Greek ends 'and we shall eat' where the Hebrew has 'in the famine'. Our Greek text gives no dictionary form; it is the future of ἐσθίω, to eat.

08.n: διεγγυάω, to give as security, to pledge.

09.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none. λημψόμεθα, 'we shall take', the future of λαμβάνω.
